title: Armored Fail Fast: The Pre-Assessment
subtitle: Take it before you feel ready.
author: Joshua
description: How to use a practice exam as a diagnosis instead of a score. Take it early and think aloud on paper, mark every answer sure, unsure or guess, sort every item into the triage grid, name the trap behind each miss, fix the principle, armor it with a reworded or reversed item, and re-measure cold. The six beliefs, the seven traps (on a test item and in written work), the eight-step route, the strategy strip, the gap lenses, and worksheets to photocopy: a think-aloud sheet, a triage grid and a trap tally. Domain-free: it works with any course's practice exam.

title: Armored Fail Fast: The Performance Assessment
subtitle: The rubric is the answer key you're allowed to see.
author: Joshua
manuscript: Armored Fail Fast - The Performance Assessment (book, V1)/Armored_Fail_Fast_2_The_Performance_Assessment.pdf
description: How to grade your own rough draft against the rubric on day one, so the first time you learn an aspect is weak is not when the evaluator tells you. Rewrite each aspect as its competent line, draft fast and complete, audit with the evaluator's eyes (no location on the page means not evident), name the mold on every weak aspect, fix the dangerous ones first, cold-read, and stop before submitting until every aspect is located and competent-and-sure. With the rubric verbs and what each demands, the ways a submission camouflages itself, a worked example on an invented vendor recommendation memo, and worksheets: the rubric self-audit, a triage grid and a trap tally. Domain-free.

title: Armored Fail Fast: The Objective Assessment
subtitle: Take it and see what happens.
author: Joshua
manuscript: Armored Fail Fast - The Objective Assessment (book, V1)/Armored_Fail_Fast_3_The_Objective_Assessment.pdf
description: The third fail-fast route: let the real exam measure you. If it passes you, you're done. If it doesn't, its coaching report tells you where, and a sounded-out pre-assessment retake tells you why. How to read the report's areas, weights and statuses, rank the areas by leverage, retake the pre-assessment one question at a time out loud, armor the flagged areas, and retake only when the drill is sure-and-right in every one. With a which-route-when table, a coaching report ledger with one column per attempt, the gap lenses and a sheet for the sounded-out retake. Domain-free.

description: The same steps as Books 1–4, told as a trail: nine breadcrumbs, each with what it gives you right away and what it becomes in every job after; what the whole trail gives you when it is walked end to end; and the branches that open from the end of it: the next course, the degree, certifications and licenses, the job search, the job itself, careers built on the method, and teaching it.
